# Verb Convention

A verb chosen by layer habit rather than by behaviour throws away the one thing the name could have
told the caller: whether there is a miss to handle. `getRoutine` and `findRoutine` then mean the same
thing in two files and different things in a third, and every call site has to open the implementation
to find out which.

The verb fills the slot in front of the `HEAD` — [naming-convention.md](./naming-convention.md#name-structure) is the structure it sits in.

## Scope

Applies to every hand-written source file — the name of a function, a method, or a class entry point.

Does **not** apply to:

- Vendor names we do not own — a third-party SDK's method names, generated clients.
- Deployment and infrastructure identifiers matched by string outside this repo.

## Verbs

The read/write vocabulary, in every layer. A stack profile may narrow this further — a repository's closed verb set, a schema action list — but never contradicts it.

> **The read verb states what happens when there is nothing to read.** `get` throws; `find` returns `null`. That is the whole distinction, and it is why a layer that never throws uses `find` throughout while a layer whose misses surface as errors uses `get`.

Reading `getRoutine(id)` you know there is no null to handle; reading `findRoutine(id)` you know there is. Choosing the verb by layer habit instead of by behaviour throws that away, and every call site then has to check the implementation to find out.

A **list** read has no missing case: an empty result is an answer, not an absence, so the read never throws and the verb is `find<Entities>` — in a repository, in a service, on the wire, in a request function alike. The layer a read sits in never decides its verb; only the behaviour does.

| Prefer                   | Meaning                                                                                | Over                                         |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `get<Entity>`            | read **one**, throws when missing                                                      | `find*`                                      |
| `find<Entity>`           | read **one**, returns `null` when missing                                              | `get*OrNull`, `lookup*`                      |
| `find<Entities>`         | read **many** — an empty result is an answer, so it never throws, in every layer       | `list*`, `getAll*`, `search*`, `fetch*`, `get<Entities>` |
| `create<Entity>`         | write a new record                                                                     | `insert*`, `save*`, `add*`, `new*`           |
| `upsert<Entity>`         | write or replace by key                                                                | `saveOrUpdate*`, `createOrUpdate*`, `merge*` |
| `update<Entity>`         | partial write — only when no domain verb fits                                          | `set*`, `patch*`, `modify*`                  |
| `delete<Entity>`         | take a record out of its store — row, cache key, document, file. Afterwards it is gone | `remove*`, `purge*`                          |
| `destroy()`              | tear down a whole object and release what it holds — connections, timers, listeners    | `close()`, `quit()`                          |
| `count<Noun>`            | cardinality                                                                            | `total*`, `num*`, `aggregate<Noun>Count`     |
| `aggregate<Noun>`        | grouped totals                                                                         | `stats*`, `sum*`, `getTotals*`               |
| `ensure<X>`              | idempotent provisioning                                                                | `createIfMissing*`, `provision*`, `init*`    |
| `handle<Event>`          | inbound event entry — `handleOrderCreated`                                             | `on<Event>`, `process<Event>`, `*Handler`    |
| `build<X>`               | pure, sync constructor of a value — `buildTrackingUrl`                                 | `make*`, `generate*`, `to*`                  |
| `resolve<X>`             | derive one value from another, may be `null`                                           | `lookup*`, `get*`                            |
| `detect<X>`              | async probe returning a fact                                                           | `check*`, `is*()`                            |
| `hydrate<X>`             | fill a result set from another source                                                  | `enrich*`, `populate*`, `decorate*`          |
| `invalidate<X>`          | cache invalidation                                                                     | `clearCache*`, `flush*`, `bust*`             |
| `run()`                  | the single entry of a script or task object                                            | `execute()`, `start()`, `process()`          |
| `<domainVerb><Entities>` | a real domain action — `archiveRoutines`, `replaceRoutine`                             | a generic `update` that hides the intent     |

## The verb carries no qualifiers

What a function does when it misses, what it is keyed by, and whether it is async are already in the verb, the parameter and the return type. Repeating any of them in the name states it a second time, and the second statement is the one that goes stale.

| Avoid                                   | Use                                                          |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `…OrThrow`, `…OrNull`                   | `get<Entity>` / `find<Entity>` — the verb already says it    |
| `…By<Field>` — `findRoutinesByProducts` | the key in the parameter — `findRoutines({ productIds })`    |
| `…Async`                                | the plain name; the return type is the signal                |
| `list*`, `get<Entities>`                | `find<Entities>` — the same verb in every layer              |

## NEVER Do

- Use `get*` for a read that returns `null`, or `find*` for a read that throws.
- Use `list*` or `get<Entities>` for a list read — it is `find<Entities>` in every layer.
- Pick a read verb by the layer it sits in rather than by whether the read can miss.
- Encode the lookup key in a method name (`…ById`, `…ByProducts`) — put it in the parameter or `filters`.
- Suffix a name with `…Async`, `…OrThrow` or `…OrNull`.
- Use `remove` or `purge` for a storage delete — it is `delete<Entity>`.
- Use `destroy()` for anything but ending an object's life, or `close()` / `quit()` on a class that has no `connect()`.
- Hide a real domain action behind a generic `update`.
